before.title: Jimny Mk3 King-Pin Bearing Wear (Front Axle Solid)
before.description: The Jimny Mk3 solid front axle uses king-pin bearings that wear, leading to vague steering, MOT failures for excessive play, and clunking from the front end. Typically presents at 80,000-150,000 km, earlier with serious off-road use. Symptoms are easy to confuse with track-rod-end or wheel-bearing wear.
before.solution: King-pin bearing kit (both sides) £100-£200 in parts; £350-£600 labor at a specialist. Use Suzuki/OEM bearings — pattern parts wear faster. Replace tracking-related components at same time (track-rod ends, drag link) since the front end is opened up.

before.title: Jimny Mk3 Chassis / Sill Corrosion (Salt-Belt)
before.description: The 1998-2018 Jimny (G/3rd gen) suffers chassis rail and sill corrosion in salt-belt markets. UK MOT failures common at 10+ years for rotted chassis sections, especially around rear axle mounts and sill structural sections. Otherwise drivetrain is famously reliable.
before.solution: Annual chassis inspection from year 7 in salt regions. Underseal/wax-cavity treatment is worth the cost. Chassis patch welding £400-£900 depending on extent. Rotted sills failing MOT can be repaired but full chassis replacement is rarely economical.

before.title: Jimny Mk4 Rear Wheel Arch / Tailgate Corrosion
before.description: The 4th-generation Jimny (2018+) shows surprisingly early rear wheel arch and tailgate corrosion, especially in salt-belt markets. Rear arches start bubbling at 3-5 years; tailgate inner skin shows blistering from inside out. UK owner forums and Honest John writeups document repeated cases under 5 years old.
before.solution: Inspect arches and tailgate inner skin annually after year 2. Underseal proactively at year 3 in salt regions. Suzuki UK has done some goodwill repairs for in-warranty cases — request inspection at dealer. Patch repair £300-£600 per arch; tailgate replacement £800-£1,500.
